desc:
Given two integer arrays a and b, build two lists:

  • the distinct values that occur in a but nowhere in b;
  • the distinct values that occur in b but nowhere in a.

Return [onlyA, onlyB], where each list is sorted in increasing order and contains no repeated value. A list may be empty.

For example, a = [1, 2, 3, 3] and b = [2, 4, 6] give [[1, 3], [4, 6]].
constraints: Both returned lists are sorted ascending without duplicates
hints: Think of each array as a set of values: you want the two one-sided set differences.
Turn both arrays into hash sets. Then A - B and B - A are exactly the two answers (before sorting).
Do not forget that the output lists must be sorted, and that duplicates inside one array must be reported only once, which a set takes care of.
editorial: Build sa = set(a) and sb = set(b). The values only in a are sa - sb and the values only in b are sb - sa. Sets already remove repeated values, and sorting each result gives the required order.

Building the sets costs O(n + m) and sorting the outputs O(n log n + m log m) in the worst case. If both arrays were already sorted you could instead merge them with two pointers and avoid hashing, but with unsorted input the set approach is simplest.
